title: Sting: Near-storage accelerator framework for scalable triangle counting and beyond
problem: Memory capacity is the critical bottleneck for scalable graph mining as graphs grow faster than DRAM scaling, while NVMe storage offers density but suffers from performance limitations.
motivation: Large graphs require efficient processing, but DRAM scaling cannot keep pace, necessitating effective use of cheaper, denser secondary storage for graph analytics.
method: STING uses asynchronous callback functions to provide a general interface to in-storage graphs, enabling transparent near-storage acceleration. The framework implements transparent filtering and sorting mechanisms at the storage layer to accelerate graph processing while minimizing data movement.
key_novelty: Asynchronous callback-based interface enabling transparent near-storage acceleration for in-storage graph processing without application-level modifications.
contributions: STING framework providing general interface to in-storage graphs via asynchronous callbacks
Transparent near-storage acceleration with filtering and sorting mechanisms
3x improvement in cost and power efficiency for triangle counting over state-of-the-art
primary_theme: Near-storage acceleration for scalable graph mining
